26Progress tab · 25a and 25b, reworked

You’re between 25a and 25b. For 25a: the dates on the right but sitting at the bottom of the title, not its top; and a version under the title, on part of a row rather than a full one. For 25b: no chevron, no drop-down menu, but its own motion to flip through the periods.

26a and 26b: on 6M, then on Program (the program’s name in place of the dates). 26c and 26d: at rest, then open. The motion for 26c and 26d is described under each; whichever you pick gets a Motion Explorations tile to try. Header as every tab; chips unchanged.

26aArrows on the title row, on the title’s baselineRejected · 26b locked
The dates and arrows sit on the same line as the bottom of “Progress”, right-aligned. Nothing added to the height.
26bArrows under the title, on part of a rowLocked · under the title
Tucked under the title on the right, overlapping the title’s row by 10px, so it takes about half a row. Reads as a caption to the title.
26cCapsule, no chevron; tap opens a small wheelRejected · 26b locked
The capsule shows the dates only. Tap: it lights blue and a wheel of periods grows down from it, newest at the bottom; flick up through older ones, the page changes as the wheel settles (the chips’ morph). Tap outside to close. A wheel, as times and durations use.
26dCapsule, no chevron; tap unrolls the periods sidewaysRejected · 26b locked
Tap: the capsule slides into a row of periods under the title, newest on the right, older ones off to the left; swipe sideways to flip, tap one to pick, and the row rolls back into the capsule. Pushes the page down one row while open.

Claude’s suggestion: 26b. You found the title row a little weird for it; under the title it reads as the title’s caption, keeps the arrows that already work, and costs only about half a row. If you’d rather drop the arrows altogether, 26d, since flipping sideways keeps their direction (older to the left). Owner (2026-11-25): “Yeah, yeah, it’s too B.” Locked: 26b. Built into the Progress Demo.

25Progress tab · the period control, redesigned

You didn’t like either place in turn 24 (“stuck in the middle there. It looks terrible”), said it would belong on the right, and that the date arrow selector needs work. All three keep the control on the right, on the title’s own row, so it scrolls away with the title.

The same in all three: the header as every tab (28px title on its own row under the top row, small title on scroll), the chips unchanged, the 6M sample. 25b and 25c are shown at rest, with the menu open, and scrolled 200px; 25a at rest and scrolled. On Program the control shows the program’s name, as today (15b). What differs: how you move to another period.

25aArrows and dates at the right of the title rowReworked in turn 26
Today’s control, one row lower, beside the title as it was. Steps one period at a time, with the locked sideways slide. Still the arrow selector you didn’t like.
25bA capsule with the dates, opening a menu of periodsReworked in turn 26
The app’s existing pick-one control (the 36pt tonal capsule and the system menu, as Rep records on Exercise detail). No arrows: tap, pick any past period, a check on the current one. The dates read as a value you can change.
25cA glass calendar button in the top row, dates as plain textRuled out (owner: “we can roll that C”)
Uses the top row kept for buttons, like Home’s gear; the dates sit quietly at the right of the title. The button stays while you scroll, so you can change period from anywhere on the page. The dates and the control are apart.

Claude’s suggestion: 25b. The dates and the control are one thing, it reuses a control the app already has, and any period is one pick away instead of several taps. Picking from the menu would change the page with the chips’ motion (charts morph, 600ms) instead of the arrows’ slide.

23Progress landing · slower, smoother period changes

After turn 22 (owner): 22a is definitely better than 22b; curious what a smoother, slower rolling transition looks like. Both phones keep 22a's idea (arrows slide by direction, chips morph) but slow it down, ease in and out, and count the numbers to their new values instead of sliding them in. For reference, 22a is 350ms (charts) and 260ms (arrows). Note the locked timing rule: smooth motion is 300–350ms; these go past it, so picking one would change that rule for this screen.

22Progress landing · motion when the period changes

Owner asked whether the charts should animate on a chip change or an arrow tap. Proposal: arrows slide by direction (Calendar's locked month flip), chips morph the charts and roll the numbers (locked "digits roll"); no haptics (the segmented control plays its own; arrows are navigation). Both phones are cut after Training to keep it light. Tap the chips and arrows.

Mock simplifications: the RPE line skips deload dots and this week's hollow dot; springs are CSS curves. In SwiftUI, Swift Charts animates data changes like this on its own. Today's Progress Demo fades the page and regrows the bars on every change, which breaks "charts grow once per visit"; it gets whichever motion you pick.

14Progress landing · paging back through periods

After turn 13 (owner): dates top right are fine (if an action button ever comes, shift things down). Owner asked for the ability to page through periods, like Whoop and Calendar: 6M starts on the latest six months and can go back to earlier ones. Comparison for an earlier window keeps the agreed rule, measured from that window: its best 3 vs the best 3 before it. Program pages by program: the current one compares like turn 11 (same block type, same point); a finished program compares with the whole program before it (the same-point comparison at 100%). The first program, and a window with nothing before it, show "–".

Mock history from Jun 2025 (six programs). Consistency and protocols per page are placeholder values. Tap the chips and the arrows.

12Progress landing · smoothing threshold, date range for the chip

After turn 11 (owner): leaning 11c; big number = average of the best 3 sessions (actual rep PRs live in Exercise detail). Smoothing changed to a rolling median of 3 (the middle of a session and the two before it: one bad or one great session is ignored, rises and drops at the same speed), with a threshold: under 8 sessions no smoothing. The 8 is a starting point to tune on device with real data. The chips no longer say what dates they cover; two places to show it.

11Progress landing · main-lift tiles on realistic data

After turn 10 (owner): the big number shouldn't be "the last couple of weeks" on every chip, and Program uses a different mechanism. Show deloads, drops, and what 1Y looks like with about 70 sessions. Here the big number follows the chip: it is the same measurement the change uses, your best 3 sessions in the range (Program: best 3 so far in Pillars 2). The change compares it with the chip's baseline, so number and change always agree. Tap the range control.

Mock history, every session, logging since Jun 2025: six programs, each block typed (Hyp, Str, Peak), a deload week (one lighter session) at the end of each, two weeks off over the holidays, Bench missing two weeks in March and coming back lighter, Overhead Press flat since Sep 7. Hyp-block sessions use higher reps, so their estimated 1RMs sit a little lower. About 70 sessions per lift in 1Y.

10Progress landing · main-lift tiles on the agreed rules

After turn 9 (owner): leaning 9a or 9b. Rules agreed: Program compares against the last block of the same type at the same point (per lift, the last time that lift was in such a block; nothing to compare = no change shown); 6M and 1Y, best 3 in the range vs the best 3 before it; All, to settle (shown here: best 3 overall vs the best 3 of the first 4 sessions).

Each piece has one job. Big number: where the lift is now (best estimated 1RM of the last couple of weeks), the same on every chip. Change: how much stronger than the comparison, same rule as the hero. Chart: the path over the range. Tap the range control on each phone. Mock: Pillars 2 is in its Hyp block, so Program compares with Pillars' Hyp block, weeks 1–3.
